title: A test set and a pass rate

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace, already pointed at the offline local model.

tasks.title: Load the test set
tasks.description:
In `src/cases.ts`, implement `loadCases(path: string): Case[]`.

`data/tickets.jsonl` holds one case per line: a JSON object with string fields `id`, `input` and `expected`. Read the file and return the cases in file order.

- Skip lines that are empty or contain only whitespace.
- Throw an `Error` whose message names the line, like `line 4`, when a line is not valid JSON or lacks a string `id`, `input` or `expected`. Count every line from 1, blank ones included, so the number matches what an editor shows.
- Throw an `Error` whose message contains the id when two cases share an id.

The check loads the shipped file and several hidden files, some of them broken on purpose.
nextSteps: Read the file as text and split it into lines.
Skip blank lines, parse the rest and keep the line number for each.
Validate each parsed value before you trust it.
Track the ids you have seen, then run `node src/run.ts` once the other tasks are done.
hints: `readFileSync(path, 'utf8')` gives you the whole file. Split on newlines and keep the index so you can report line numbers.
`JSON.parse` throws on bad input. Catch that and throw your own error that says which line it was.
The line number is the array index plus one, counted before you skip blank lines. A `Set` of ids tells you when one repeats.

tasks.title: Compare labels fairly
tasks.description:
The triage model does not always format its label the same way. In `src/evaluate.ts`, implement:

- `normalizeLabel(text: string): string`: trim, lowercase, drop a leading `category:` label, drop quotes or backticks around the label, drop trailing `.` or `!`, and turn every run of spaces or underscores inside the label into a single `-`. So `'  Category: "Plant care"  '` becomes `'plant-care'`.
- `isExactMatch(output: string, expected: string): boolean`: normalize both sides, then compare them exactly. A reply that only contains the expected word, like `'not a refund'`, is not a match.

The check runs both functions on a hidden list of replies.
nextSteps: Run `node src/run.ts` once task 3 works and read the raw labels the model sends.
Write `normalizeLabel` one rule at a time, in the order the task lists them.
hints: Normalization fixes formatting, not meaning. Every rule should remove noise without changing which word the model chose.
A chain of `.replace()` calls with small regular expressions keeps each rule on its own line. Anchor them with `^` and `$` so you only touch the edges.
Trim again after removing the prefix and the punctuation, then replace `/[\s_]+/g` last.

tasks.title: Score a model on the test set
tasks.description:
In `src/evaluate.ts`, implement `runEval(cases: Case[], model: string): Promise<EvalReport>`.

Send each case's `input` through `triage(input, model)` and return:

- `model`: the model name you were given
- `total`: the number of cases
- `passed`: how many replies match `expected` with `isExactMatch`
- `passRate`: `passed / total`, or `0` when there are no cases
- `failures`: one `{ id, expected, got }` per missed case, in case order, where `got` is the normalized reply and `expected` is the case's value

The check runs your function on hidden cases with two different models and with an empty list.
nextSteps: Loop over the cases and await `triage` for each one.
Normalize the reply and decide whether the case passed.
Collect the failures and compute the totals.
hints: Use the model name you are given. The check calls runEval with two different models and expects different results.
Keep a `failures` array and push to it inside the loop. `passed` is then the total minus the number of failures.
Guard the division: when `total` is 0, `passRate` should be 0, not `NaN`.
